title: Proofs 6-7; against Vorstius on diversity in life
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): plus attribute to God those things whose likeness exists in creatures only with ye mode belonging toward supereminence plus negation belonging toward every imperfection — but they wisely know who know divine things well. 247, saying it seems some diversity stands as in God, so that same one thing stands as God's living substance itself, another ye life or force by means belonging toward that same which He lives. Here also Conrad Vorstius departs in Notes on Disputation III p. that same stands as an immortal living being — zeno belonging toward Citium called God an animal. Hermes; Orpheus; Therefore life plus continuous eternal age stand as in God. We say therefore that same God stands as a living being everlasting plus best. Aristotle, Metaphysics XII: SEVENTH, ye Gentile philosophers subscribe. because God stands as indeed ye highest life plus Himself ye fountain belonging toward life — there stands as no life that same stands as not out from God. Augustine: Basil ye Great; plus indeed that same He live plus can grant life to those in whom He wills life to be — there must be in ye true God incorruption plus freedom out from destruction. Cyril belonging toward Alexandria: God stands as life plus incorruption plus truth. pass_b_english: SIXTH, to these is added the consent of orthodox antiquity. To Dionysius named from the Areopagus God is self-life and living through Himself, eternally living; and with him Gregory, the archetypal author of life. Irenaeus: God is life and incorruption and truth. Cyril of Alexandria: There must be in the true God incorruption and freedom from destruction, and indeed that He live and can grant life to those in whom He wills life to be. Basil the Great; Augustine: There is no life that is not from God, because God is indeed the highest life and Himself the fountain of life.

SEVENTH, the Gentile philosophers subscribe. Aristotle, Metaphysics XII: We say therefore that God is a living being everlasting and best. Therefore life and continuous eternal age are in God. Orpheus; Hermes; Zeno of Citium called God an animal, that is an immortal living being.

Here also Conrad Vorstius departs in Notes on Disputation III p. 247, saying it seems some diversity is in God, so that one thing is God's living substance itself, another the life or force by which He lives. But they wisely know who know divine things well, and attribute to God those things whose likeness exists in creatures only with the mode of supereminence and negation of every imperfection.
source_text: SEXTO, his accedit consensus orthodoxae antiquitatis. Dionysio qui ab Areopago denominatur Deus est autzoe, ipsavita et autzoos per se vivens, aeizoon aeternum vivens; et juxta cum hoc Gregorio, archezoon vitae auctor. Irenaeus: Deus vita est et incorruptela et veritas. Cyrillus Alexandrinus: Inest, inquit, oportet vero Deo incorruptio et interitus vacuitas, imo et ut vivat, et vitam tribuere possit his quibus vitam velit inesse. Basilius Magnus; Augustinus: Nulla vita est quae non sit ex Deo, quia Deus utique summa vita est et ipse fons vitae. SEPTIMO, subscribunt philosophi gentiles. Aristoteles Metaph. XII: Dicimus itaque Deum sempiternum optimumque vivens esse. Quare vita et aevum continuum et aeternum Deo inest. Orpheus; Hermes; Zeno Cittieus Deum animal dixit, id est vivens immortale. DISCEDIT hic etiam Conradus Vorstius Notis ad disp. III p.247, inquiens videri aliquid in Deo diversitatis inesse, ut aliud sit ipsa Dei substantia vivens, aliud vita seu vis illa per quam vivit. Sed modeste sapiunt qui res divinas bene sapiunt, nec Deo tribuunt ea quorum similitudo in creaturis exstat, nisi cum modo supereminentiae ac negatione omnimodae imperfectionis.
